name: software_repo_growth

feature_docs.created_today: 1 if the repository was created today [raw]
feature_docs.created_yesterday: 1 if the repository was created the previous day [raw]

target: stars received by the repository on the next day (non-bot accounts)

identification.statement: Associations in public GitHub activity; nothing was randomized.

population: public GitHub accounts and public repositories whose events reached GitHub's public events API and GH Archive between 2024-10-07 and 2024-10-10 UTC (Monday to Thursday); bot accounts excluded from units

selection.rule: lowest validation mean Poisson deviance; confirmed on test by paired bootstrap

dispersion.fitted_on: train rows, kept model means, maximum likelihood

limits: Population: public GitHub, 2024-10-07..10 UTC (four weekdays of one autumn week). Developers on GitHub are skewed towards professional, English-speaking and North-American/European/Asian time zones; private repositories and private activity are invisible. GH Archive records the public events API, which drops events under load and omits some activity; counts are lower bounds. Stars are cheap signals inflated by automation and star farming; a star is not evidence of useful adoption (MASTER_SPEC 6.5). These models describe engagement dynamics, not usefulness. Observational associations only: nothing was randomized, so the models do not say what promotion, ranking or buying stars would cause. Short horizon: features look back 24 h and outcomes forward 24 h; long-run adoption, retention, maintenance and dependency incorporation are not observed. Bots are identified only by the '[bot]' login suffix; other automation accounts remain in the data. Units are repositories with at least one star or fork on the day (or created that day): the model says nothing about the large majority of repositories with no such activity. Next-day stars for the test day (2024-10-10) come from a Thursday; weekday and holiday patterns are not modelled. The negative-binomial dispersion was fitted on training rows; the simulated distribution's tail (q99.9) should be compared with the report before using the model for viral outliers.

simulator_mapping.unit: a repository (or package) in the software ecosystem on one simulated day
simulator_mapping.stars_today: star/watch actions by developers on the repository today
simulator_mapping.issue_events_today: issue tracker events on its project today
simulator_mapping.output: expected stars tomorrow; sample(rng, X) draws counts with the fitted NB2 dispersion
simulator_mapping.use: a reference for the rate at which simulated developers discover repositories (to validate or calibrate the simulator's discovery and recommendation mechanisms), not a creator-assigned popularity
simulator_mapping.transform: matrix_from_counts(raw) applies log1p to count features
